findings.claim: Early sections correctly render "route accuracy" as "Routengenauigkeit". From the experiments section onward it becomes "Routenpräzision" in the bullet list, the live-scoring paragraph, an H2 and the paragraph that follows. In ML German, Präzision means precision, a different metric from accuracy. The scorer (`route-accuracy`) computes exact-match accuracy. The switch is technically misleading and inconsistent within the text.
findings.suggestion: Use "Routengenauigkeit" everywhere, including the H2: "## Was nach der Routengenauigkeit zu messen ist".

findings.claim: Accuracy becomes Präzision here and throughout the later sections, despite being translated earlier as Routengenauigkeit. In a classification tutorial, accuracy and precision can denote different metrics. The supplied scorer measures whether each selected route matches the expected route, so this terminology obscures exactly what the reported number means.
findings.suggestion: Use Routengenauigkeit consistently: „Der alte Router erzielte bei der Routengenauigkeit `0.94`.“ Replace subsequent instances of Routenpräzision, including the heading. Preserve the numerical values and code identifiers.

findings.claim: These nonadjacent passages show the unexplained shift from du in the introduction to Sie in the instructional body. Either form can work in German, but this mid-article change makes the voice feel assembled from inconsistent translations.

The change preserves the established conversational distance; it does not require a claim that formal German is inherently unsuitable.

findings.claim: Die ganze Narbe suggests one strangely quantified scar. The source evokes accumulated painful production experience, with a deliberately physical, dry metaphor.
findings.suggestion: „Unter ‚Sonstiges‘ sammeln sich die Narben aus dem Produktionsbetrieb.“ This replaces the literal tissue image with idiomatic plural scars. It loses the anatomical specificity of scar tissue and gains natural German while retaining accumulated damage and the author's edge.

findings.quote: anspruchsvoller Code oder beweisintensive Analyse

votes.reason: The target says „Der alte Router erzielte eine Routenpräzision von `0.94`“, while the source says "scored `0.94` on route accuracy". The scorer shown computes exact-match agreement ("decision.route === expected.route ? 1 : 0"), which is accuracy, not precision. Earlier the target correctly uses „Routengenauigkeit“. In an evals tutorial, putting the reported numbers under the wrong metric is a technical error, not just inconsistent wording. The same wrong term also appears in an H2 and in the live-scoring paragraph. I first rated this 3, but I accept 4 because it misstates what the key numbers measure.

The target opens with du („Sobald du einen Router hinzufügst“, „dein System“). From „raten Sie über die eigentliche Entscheidung“ onward it uses Sie for the rest of the article, including „Bewerten Sie die Entscheidung“ and „beginnen Sie hier“. The switch has no rhetorical reason. It affects most of the article and pushes the voice toward the sanitized vendor tone the brief rules out. Because it is so widespread, I rate it 4 rather than 3.

„In „Sonstiges“ steckt die ganze Narbe aus dem Produktionsbetrieb“ uses an odd singular with a quantifier. It does not carry the source's idea of scar tissue built up over time („production scar tissue“). This line is the author's dry punchline, so a clumsy version hurts the voice. That makes it 3, not 2. The fix is to use „Narben“ in the plural or to adapt the image as Lehrgeld.

„Mit dem Dataset [`dataset.startExperiment()`](…) können Sie es … ausführen“ reads as if the method call were the dataset's name, and „es“ has no clear referent. The source separates the precondition („With the dataset in place“) from the operation. This sentence introduces the section's main API, so it needs to be restructured. The URL and identifier must stay unchanged.

„raten Sie über die eigentliche Entscheidung“ is not idiomatic German. Natural options are „über etwas rätseln/mutmaßen“ or „etwas nur erraten können“. It is the first sentence of the section and its core claim, so native readers will notice it. The fix can be combined with the du repair.

„beweisintensive Analyse“ renders "evidence-heavy analysis". „Beweis“ can mean evidence in a legal sense, so it is not strictly wrong. In a developer context, though, it leans toward formal proofs. It also breaks consistency with „Belege“, which the target uses elsewhere („ohne Belege zu bewahren“). This is minor polish in a table cell and does not change the meaning, so I rate it 2, not 3.

„Die erste Routing-Eingabeaufforderung“ uses the German name for the Windows command prompt. Everywhere else the text uses „Prompt“ („Router-Prompt“, „präziseren Prompt“). It is a real stray term, but it appears once and the meaning can be recovered from context, so I rate it 2 as polish rather than 3.

„Bekämpfe Übel mit Evals!“ verliert das lautliche Wortspiel von „Fight Evils with Evals!“ und klingt im Deutschen steif. „dein System“ gegenüber dem späteren „Ihr Produkt“ belegt den übergreifenden Anredebruch und trägt die hohe Priorität. „Routing-Eingabeaufforderung“ gegenüber „Router-Prompt“ ist zusätzlich kleinere Terminologiepflege. The du-to-Sie switch mid-article is confirmed in the target and reads inconsistent for a German dev blog. Die Quelle nennt die Kennzahl „route accuracy“; das Ziel wechselt von „Routengenauigkeit“ zu „Routenpräzision“. Precision und Accuracy sind unterschiedliche Klassifikationsmetriken; hier sollte durchgehend „Routengenauigkeit“ stehen. Außerdem macht „Mit dem Dataset `dataset.startExperiment()`“ den Methodenaufruf sprachlich zum Dataset. Die Quelle unterscheidet beides: „With the dataset in place, […] runs it“. Besser: „Sobald das Dataset steht, führt `dataset.startExperiment()` es gegen einen registrierten Agenten, Workflow oder Scorer aus.“ Der erhaltene Code behebt diese Fehler in der Erklärung nicht.

Two real problems. First, the sentence is broken. The target has "Mit dem Dataset [`dataset.startExperiment()`] können Sie es … ausführen", which puts the method call in apposition to "Dataset", as if the call were the dataset. The source says "With the dataset in place, `dataset.startExperiment()` runs it". Suggested fix: "Steht das Dataset, führt `dataset.startExperiment()` es gegen einen registrierten Agenten, Workflow oder Scorer aus." Second, the metric name drifts. The target first uses "Routengenauigkeit", then switches to "Routenpräzision" ("erzielte eine Routenpräzision von `0.94`", plus the heading "Was nach der Routenpräzision zu messen ist"). The source only says "route accuracy", and the scorer id is `route-accuracy`. In evals, accuracy and precision are different metrics, so the reported number gets the wrong label. Use "Routengenauigkeit" throughout.

Source 'route accuracy' becomes 'Routenpräzision' after initially being translated as 'Routengenauigkeit'. This introduces a misleading metric distinction; consistently use 'Routengenauigkeit'. Also, 'Mit dem Dataset `dataset.startExperiment()`' identifies the method as the dataset, whereas the source says the method 'runs it against a registered agent, workflow, or scorer'. Repair: 'Mit `dataset.startExperiment()` führst du das Dataset gegen einen registrierten Agenten, Workflow oder Scorer aus.' These are translation defects, independent of API compatibility.

The quoted sentence is an acceptable rendering of the source: "With the dataset in place, `dataset.startExperiment()` runs it against…". It does not misidentify the method call as a dataset, so that half of the claim is unfounded. The metric half is valid. Source "route accuracy" is rendered "Routengenauigkeit" early on, matching the `route-accuracy` scorer. Later it becomes "Der alte Router erzielte eine Routenpräzision von `0.94`" and "Was nach der Routenpräzision zu messen ist". In ML, Präzision means precision, a different metric from accuracy. For German developers this is a real terminology error, and it makes one central concept appear under two names. It needs to be unified to Routengenauigkeit. Blocking because it affects technical meaning.

Separately, "beweisintensive Analyse" for "evidence-heavy analysis" sounds machine-translated, and it also clashes with "Belege", which the target uses elsewhere. "belegintensive Analyse" fits better. Both are noticeable style problems. Neither changes meaning, and the "Bauchgefühl mit Dispatch-Tabelle" joke still lands.

The target establishes 'Sobald du einen Router hinzufügst' and 'dein System', then changes to 'raten Sie', 'Geben Sie' and sustained formal address through the checklist. findings.claim: The intro and first H2 use du ("Sobald du einen Router hinzufügst", "dein System"). From "Die Router-Entscheidung bewertbar machen" to the end, every imperative and pronoun is Sie. findings.claim: Early sections correctly render "route accuracy" as "Routengenauigkeit". From the experiments section onward it becomes "Routenpräzision" in the bullet list, the live-scoring paragraph, an H2 and the paragraph that follows. In ML German, Präzision means precision, a different metric from accuracy. The scorer (`route-accuracy`) computes exact-match accuracy. The switch is technically misleading and inconsistent within the text.
findings.suggestion: Use "Routengenauigkeit" everywhere, including the H2: "## Was nach der Routengenauigkeit zu messen ist".

changes.sourceQuote:
If you are building a Mastra router today, start here:

1. Make the routing decision structured, even if users never see it.
2. Write deterministic scorers for valid JSON, expected route, and forbidden routes.
3. Use `runEvals` with 10 to 20 cases before changing router prompts or models.
4. Promote real failures into a versioned dataset.
5. Run dataset experiments for meaningful prompt, model, route, or workflow changes.
6. Add live scorers for cheap production invariants.
7. Compare experiments by route, not only by average score.

Code einschließlich ausführbarer Prompts und Kommentare, Backtick-Begriffe, Mengen, URLs, Frontmatter, Assets und Abschnittsstruktur werden durch die Ersetzungen erhalten. Quellprobleme werden nicht stillschweigend repariert. If you are building a Mastra router today, start here:

1. Make the routing decision structured, even if users never see it.
2. Write deterministic scorers for valid JSON, expected route, and forbidden routes.
3. Use `runEvals` with 10 to 20 cases before changing router prompts or models.
4. Promote real failures into a versioned dataset.
5. Run dataset experiments for meaningful prompt, model, route, or workflow changes.
6. Add live scorers for cheap production invariants.
7. Compare experiments by route, not only by average score.

revision.explanation: Die Ersetzungen sind exakt und nicht überlappend. Sie beheben alle belegten Blocker: durchgängige du-Ansprache, Routengenauigkeit an allen vier bisherigen Präzisionsstellen sowie die missverständliche Einführung von `dataset.startExperiment()`. Die sichtbaren mittleren Formulierungsprobleme bei „raten über“, „die ganze Narbe“, „beweisintensive Analyse“ und „Routing-Eingabeaufforderung“ sind ebenfalls repariert. Redaktionelle Selbsteinschätzung nach diesen Ersetzungen: Lesbarkeit, Autorenstimme und lokale Angemessenheit jeweils mindestens 4/5; keine ungelösten mittleren Übersetzungsdefekte. Die Beanstandungen zu „Die Fehler stecken im Ablauf“ (93a25c43c6d480ab9a8c) und „langweilige Schnittstellen“ (dc304a8a8a01770f1d15) rechtfertigen keine Pflichtänderung: Beide vermitteln ihre Funktion verständlich. Auch „mit Evidenz zu argumentieren“ (8121b45e65749add4391) ist im technischen Kontext verständlich; die pauschale Zurückweisung als falscher Freund trägt nicht. Code einschließlich ausführbarer Prompts und Kommentare, Backtick-Begriffe, Mengen, URLs, Frontmatter, Assets und Abschnittsstruktur werden durch die Ersetzungen erhalten. Quellprobleme werden nicht stillschweigend repariert. Die evidenceIds bleiben leer, weil keine geprüften Referenzen mitgeliefert wurden; jede Änderung nennt stattdessen ihren wörtlichen Quellenbeleg.

If you are building a Mastra router today, start here:

1. Make the routing decision structured, even if users never see it.
2. Write deterministic scorers for valid JSON, expected route, and forbidden routes.
3. Use `runEvals` with 10 to 20 cases before changing router prompts or models.
4. Promote real failures into a versioned dataset.
5. Run dataset experiments for meaningful prompt, model, route, or workflow changes.
6. Add live scorers for cheap production invariants.
7. Compare experiments by route, not only by average score.

changes.sourceQuote:
If you are building a Mastra router today, start here:

1. Make the routing decision structured, even if users never see it.
2. Write deterministic scorers for valid JSON, expected route, and forbidden routes.
3. Use `runEvals` with 10 to 20 cases before changing router prompts or models.
4. Promote real failures into a versioned dataset.
5. Run dataset experiments for meaningful prompt, model, route, or workflow changes.
